title: He hit better both years and still lost
description:
David Justice had a higher batting average than Derek Jeter in 1995 (.253 vs .250) and in 1996 (.321 vs .314), yet over both years Jeter wins easily, .310 to .270. The trick is where the at-bats fell: Jeter had 582 of his 630 at-bats in 1996, the year both hit well, while Justice had 411 of his 551 in 1995, the year both hit worse. Give them the same at-bats each season and Justice leads, .287 to .282. This is Simpson's paradox: a total can flip the winner of every part.

Numbers checked in code (every average, the equal-weight comparison, and 100,000 simulated replays of both seasons). Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox (Ken Ross, A Mathematician at the Ballpark, 2004; Baseball-Reference.com).
